function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

We can use the cmd_controller_execute function to run a command that checks if the script is running. On Windows, we can use tasklist or wmic. For example: tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq python.exe" /FI "WINDOWTITLE eq d:/playground/pc_contoller/v2.py". But the script might be running under python interpreter. We can check for python processes and maybe check command line arguments. Use wmic process where name='python.exe' get CommandLine. Or use powershell: Get-Process -Name python | Where-Object {$_.Path -eq 'd:/playground/pc_contoller/v2.py'} but python path is not the script path. Instead, we can check command line: wmic process where "name='python.exe'" get CommandLine. Then parse. So we can run: wmic process where "name='python.exe'" get CommandLine.
